summary: This program takes a string with a jumble of capital and lowercase letters and prints an all-capitals version of it using Python's built-in `upper()` method.

lines.text: The quotes are what make this a string, and Python keeps the letters exactly as typed, mixed cases and all, until you ask for something different.

`upper()` is a method that belongs to the string itself, which is why it is written after a dot on `text`. It returns a brand-new uppercase string rather than changing `text`, so the result has to be stored in a variable to be of any use.
Printing the new variable shows I LOVE PUPPIES; printing `text` here instead would still give the original mixed-case version, since strings in Python cannot be modified in place.
